test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-4) Official paper (Held On: 10 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Ram and Dipti each invested a sum of Rs. 8000 for a period of two years at 30% compound interest per annum. However, while for Ram the interest was compounded annually, for Dipti it was compounded every eight months. How much more will Dipti receive as interest compared to Ram at the end of the two-year period?
solution:
**Given:**

Ram and Dipti each invested a sum of Rs. 8000 for a period of two years at 30% compound interest per annum.

Rate of interest of Ram is compound annually

Rate of interest of Dipti is compounded every eight months

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculation:**

When rate of interest is compounded eight months of Dipti = (30 × 8/12)%

⇒ 20%

Time for Dipti = (2 × 12/8) = 3 years

Now,

CI for Ram is 

⇒ A = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ A = 8000(1 + 30/100)²

⇒ 8000(1 + 3/10)²

⇒ (8000 × 13/10 × 13/10)

⇒ (80 × 169)

⇒ 13,520

Interest = A – P

⇒ Rs. (13,520 – 8000)

⇒ Rs. 5520

Now,

CI for Dipti is

⇒ A = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ A = 8000(1 + 20/100)³

⇒ 8000(1 + 1/5)³

⇒ 8000(6/5)³

⇒ (8000 × 216/125)

⇒ (64 × 216)

⇒ 13,824

Interest = A – P

⇒ Rs. (13,824 – 8000)

⇒ Rs. 5824

Now,

Dipti receive as interest compared to Ram at the end of the two-year period = Rs. (5824 – 5520)

⇒ Rs. 304

**∴ The required interest is Rs. 304**
